items.both_sides: Behind the onset, MT 12:25 ends on the utterance signature (נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה) and a petuchah is recorded after that verse; in front of it MT 12:26 is a strict word-event onset, one of the 39 verses carrying the contiguous form, and the formula is the whole verse (וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר). At the close, MT 12:28 ends on the same signature (נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה) with a setumah recorded after that verse, while MT 13:1 carries a fresh strict word-event onset in the same five words. Each seam is therefore a refrain-grade close followed by a full onset, and a three-verse span sits at the over-split floor because this is a complete word-event unit, which is the condition the floor states. The disputed device labels touch neither seam, so the span itself stands.

suggested_fix.fact: the proverb token the genre label rests on stands outside this span, at MT 12:22 and MT 12:23; the counted devices the span does carry are the son-of-man address at MT 12:27 and the messenger formula at MT 12:28

items.claim: The row's mark disclosure names MT 13:7 as the hailstone-storm verse, but MT 13:7 is the false-vision denial (הֲל֤וֹא מַֽחֲזֵה שָׁוְא֙ חֲזִיתֶ֔ם) and the hailstones stand at MT 13:11 (אַבְנֵ֤י אֶלְגָּבִישׁ֙) and MT 13:13 (וְאַבְנֵ֥י אֶלְגָּבִ֖ישׁ), both outside this row; the same transposition drives the rejected alternative's storm-verdict label for MT 13:8-9. Three device facts inside the span go undisclosed: MT 13:8 ends on the verse-final utterance signature (נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה), one of the 81 verses carrying it, and MT 13:6 and MT 13:7 each carry the short utterance form (נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה), two of only four verses in the book that do.
items.both_sides: Behind the onset, MT 12:28 ends on the utterance signature with a setumah recorded after that verse; in front of it MT 13:1 is a strict word-event onset and the formula is the whole verse, so the near seam is a refrain-grade close followed by a full onset. At the interior point the row declines, the setumah is recorded after MT 13:7 and MT 13:8 opens on the messenger formula; a messenger formula is a sub-onset only where the addressee changes or a close stands before it. The addressee does not change, because the second-person plural of MT 13:5 and MT 13:7 runs straight into the second-person plural of MT 13:8, so the row's stated reason is right on the bytes. The other branch of that test turns on MT 13:7's short utterance form, which sits inside the false prophets' own quoted speech and so carries no divine close; that is precisely why the verse has to be named and qualified rather than passed over in silence. At the close, MT 13:9 ends on a recognition-type clause whose divine-name pair (וִידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֥י אֲנִ֖י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה) keeps it outside the 64-verse wider recognition family as well as outside the strict 28, so the row's weaker-close reading there is correct and byte-grounded.

suggested_fix.fact: the setumah follows the false-vision denial at MT 13:7 and not a hailstone verse; the hailstones stand at MT 13:11 and MT 13:13, and MT 13:7 also carries the short utterance form inside the false prophets' quoted speech, which is the fact that completes the row's reason for declining a seam at MT 13:8

items.claim: MT 14:21 opens on the messenger formula (כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה), one of the 122 verses carrying it, yet the row declines an interior seam at MT 14:20/14:21 on the express ground that MT 14:21 introduces no fresh messenger onset. A petuchah is recorded after MT 14:20, whose oath carries the utterance signature (חַי אָ֗נִי נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה), and the address turns to direct second-person plural at MT 14:22 (וּרְאִיתֶ֥ם) and MT 14:23 (וְנִחֲמ֣וּ אֶתְכֶ֔ם). The row further asserts four times that a refrain list is not cut inside, a treatment whose ruled scope is a closed set of measured and enumerated blocks in the temple, trade, underworld-roster and tribal-allotment passages, none of them in this chapter; and it labels the signature at MT 14:16, MT 14:18 and MT 14:20 a verse close when in each of those three it stands inside the oath mid-verse, only MT 14:14 (נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה) and MT 14:23 carrying it verse-final. The son-of-man address at MT 14:13 (בֶּן אָדָ֗ם) is undisclosed.
items.both_sides: For the seam: MT 14:20 ends the fourth hypothetical on the oath with the utterance signature attached; the petuchah after MT 14:20 is the only interior parashah mark in the span and is an open rather than a closed section; MT 14:21 opens on a counted messenger formula; and the addressee changes from the third-person hypothetical land of MT 14:13-20 to the exiles addressed directly at MT 14:22-23. A messenger formula is a sub-onset where the addressee changes or a close stands before it, and here both conditions hold, and a refrain-grade close followed by a sub-onset is a seam candidate. The span is 12 verses against a target of 7 to 10, and the wider allowance is ruled for the measured and listed blocks of the temple and allotment chapters rather than for this one. Against the seam: MT 14:21 opens with a subordinating 'for', and the four scourges it names are the same four rehearsed at MT 14:13-19, so MT 14:21-23 reads as the application of the preceding hypothesis rather than as a new oracle; there is no word-event onset at MT 14:21; and a resulting three-verse row would sit at the over-split floor without being a complete word-event unit, which is the condition the floor's own named three-verse precedent satisfies. Either way the row's stated ground cannot stand: if the controlling reading keeps the span whole on that continuity, the messenger formula at MT 14:21 must still be disclosed and the level cannot remain high on a rejected alternative that denies it. The outer seams are sound and are not in question: a petuchah after MT 14:11 with the utterance signature on that verse, a strict word-event onset at MT 14:12, the utterance signature verse-final at MT 14:23 (נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה) with a petuchah after it, and a fresh strict word-event onset at MT 15:1.

suggested_fix.fact: MT 14:21 opens on the messenger formula, a counted member of the 122-verse family, with a petuchah recorded after MT 14:20 and the address turning to the second person plural at MT 14:22-23; the seam at MT 14:20/14:21 is therefore a live interior candidate and the denial of a messenger onset at that verse is false on its bytes
